input.command:
import RNA
seqs = {}
name=None
for line in open('/fixtures/rna.fasta'):
    line=line.strip()
    if not line: continue
    if line.startswith('>'): name=line[1:]; seqs[name]=''
    else: seqs[name]+=line

print("ViennaRNA", RNA.__version__, "| params: Turner 2004 (default)")
results={}
for n,s in seqs.items():
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(s)
    ss, mfe = fc.mfe()
    fc.exp_params_rescale(mfe)
    pf_ss, gfe = fc.pf()                      # ensemble free energy
    cen, dist = fc.centroid()
    cen_e = fc.eval_structure(cen)
    mea_ss, mea = fc.MEA()
    p_mfe = fc.pr_structure(ss)
    ed = fc.ensemble_defect(ss)
    results[n]=dict(seq=s,ss=ss,mfe=mfe,gfe=gfe,cen=cen,cen_e=cen_e,dist=dist,
                    mea_ss=mea_ss,mea=mea,p_mfe=p_mfe,ed=ed,
                    diversity=fc.mean_bp_distance())
    print(f"\n=== {n} ({len(s)} nt) ===")
    print(s)
    print(ss, f" MFE = {mfe:.2f} kcal/mol")
    print(f"  ensemble free energy G = {gfe:.2f} kcal/mol")
    print(f"  P(MFE structure)       = {p_mfe:.4f}  ({p_mfe*100:.2f}%)")
    print(f"  ensemble defect        = {ed:.3f} nt  ({100*ed/len(s):.1f}% of nts)")
    print(f"  mean bp distance (diversity) = {fc.mean_bp_distance():.2f}")
    print(f"  centroid: {cen}  d={dist:.2f}  E={cen_e:.2f}")
    print(f"  MEA     : {mea_ss}  MEA={mea:.2f}")
    print(f"  centroid == MFE ? {cen==ss}   MEA == MFE ? {mea_ss==ss}")

content.text: The feature tool's energies are crude heuristics that disagree with ViennaRNA; let me verify one number I mislabeled (ensemble defect units) before reporting.

Confirmed — `ensemble_defect()` returns the **normalized** fraction, so the tRNA figure is 45.3%, not 0.6% (my intermediate print mislabeled the units).

## What I ran

- Read `/fixtures/rna.fasta` (2 records) via the Python REPL.
- Folded both with **ViennaRNA 2.7.2** Python bindings, Turner 2004 parameters, 37 °C, no dangles override: `mfe()`, `pf()` (partition function), `centroid()`, `MEA()`, `pr_structure()`, `ensemble_defect()`, `subopt(Δ=10 kcal/mol)`.
- Cross-checked topology with `analyze_rna_secondary_structure_features` (biomni). Its base-pair/stem/loop counts agree with mine; **its free energies do not** (it reported −24.60 and −32.90 kcal/mol) — that tool uses a crude additive heuristic, so all energies below are ViennaRNA's.

## Results

**`hairpin_test` (38 nt)**
```
GGGAAAUCCCGCGCUUCGGCGCGGGAUUUCCCAAAAAA
((((((((((((((....))))))))))))))......   MFE = -30.50 kcal/mol
```
Ensemble ΔG = −30.51 · P(MFE) = **99.08%** · ensemble defect 0.1% · mean bp distance 0.02 · gap to 2nd-best = **3.70 kcal/mol** (only 68 structures within 10 kcal/mol). Centroid and MEA structures are *identical* to the MFE. One helix, 14 bp, one loop: a **cUUCGg tetraloop** (the canonical hyperstable UNCG motif) plus a 6-nt unpaired 3′ A-tail.

**`trna_like` (76 nt)**
```
GCGGAUUUAGCUCAGUUGGGAGAGCGCCAGACUGAAGAUCUGGAGGUCCUGUGUUCGAUCCACAGAAUUCGCACCA
(((((((..((((........)))).(((((.......))))).....(((((.......))))))))))))....   MFE = -22.40 kcal/mol
```
Ensemble ΔG = −24.13 · P(MFE) = **6.07%** · ensemble defect 45.3% · mean bp distance 23.38 · gap to 2nd-best = **0.30 kcal/mol** (303,013 structures within 10 kcal/mol). Centroid (−3.01) and MEA structures both differ from the MFE. **4 helices, 21 bp, 3 hairpin loops** — the classic tRNA cloverleaf (acceptor + D + anticodon + T arms).

## Two caveats on the question as posed

1. **`trna_like` isn't a hairpin.** It's a four-helix cloverleaf, so the comparison isn't hairpin-vs-hairpin — it's one clean hairpin vs. a multi-branch fold. If you specifically want its *best single hairpin*, the T-arm and anticodon arms are 5 bp each (~−8 kcal/mol by the heuristic tool), far weaker than `hairpin_test`'s single 14-bp stem.
2. **Don't rank these on raw MFE.** `hairpin_test` wins on total MFE (−30.50 vs −22.40) but it's also half the length; per-nucleotide it's −0.80 vs −0.30 kcal/mol/nt. The length-independent evidence — P(MFE), ensemble defect, energy gap, centroid/MEA agreement — all points the same way, which is what actually makes the call robust.

I recognize `trna_like` as yeast tRNA-Phe (the 1EHZ/4TNA sequence) from memory — I did not BLAST it, so treat that identification as unverified; say the word and I'll run `blast_sequence` to confirm.

## ANSWER

**`hairpin_test` forms the far cleaner hairpin.**

| | hairpin_test (38 nt) | trna_like (76 nt) |
|---|---|---|
| MFE | **−30.50 kcal/mol** | **−22.40 kcal/mol** |
| Ensemble free energy | −30.51 kcal/mol | −24.13 kcal/mol |
| P(MFE structure) | 99.08% | 6.07% |
| Energy gap to 2nd-best | 3.70 kcal/mol | 0.30 kcal/mol |
| Ensemble defect | 0.1% | 45.3% |
| Topology | 1 helix, 14 bp, UUCG tetraloop | 4 helices, 21 bp (cloverleaf — not a hairpin) |

`hairpin_test` is a single, essentially unique 14-bp stem–UUCG-tetraloop whose MFE, centroid and MEA structures all coincide. `trna_like` folds to a four-arm cloverleaf with a flat, degenerate ensemble. (All energies: ViennaRNA 2.7.2, Turner 2004, 37 °C.)
